text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — High error-rate on /api/v1/generate; 5xx % jumped to ~12% across us-west; paging eng-oncall (PD incident #INC-4821)
Jamal H.: oncall here, looking now. any customer impact reported?
Sophie L.: support getting a couple of customer reports: timeouts + 502s for some burst requests, not widespread yet but one enterprise trial hit it hard.
Alex P.: seeing gateway 502 and 504 from our edge -> upstream pools showing increased latency. Root cause unknown, could be provider-side throttling or KV cache pressure.
Kevin T.: I can check infra quickly — checking the gateway and pool health.
opsbot: logs tail: 
```
2026-03-15T10:12:05Z gateway: upstream resp 502 service=gpt-pool-3 latency=321ms
2026-03-15T10:12:06Z runtime: call timeout error: context deadline exceeded
2026-03-15T10:12:09Z gateway: upstream resp 504 service=gpt-pool-2 latency=1500ms
```
Jamal H.: mitigation plan: 1) route traffic away from pools with highest 5xx, 2) increase request timeout for frontend to avoid cascading retries, 3) temporarily silence noisy alert if it's paged on every spike.
Maria G.: customers affected: two trials + a small subset of API keys had increased error rate. We should notify CSMs if this persists >30m.
Alex P.: I'm running an immediate canary fallback to smaller model variant for /api/v1/generate to reduce load. Command: `rbctl route set --route /api/v1/generate --fallback gpt-medium-v2`
Kevin T.: evicting gpt-pool-3 from routing; rebalancing. Also seeing EC2 spot churn in that AZ — might be upstream provider preemptions.
Sophie L.: flagging customers A and B — sending interim message saying we're investigating.
Jamal H.: changing frontend timeout from 30s to 45s to allow retries to complete gracefully: `k apply -f frontend-timeout-patch.yaml` — done.
Alex P.: pushing temporary alert mute for the 5xx paging rule (rule: alerts/5xx-high) — muting for 20m while we stabilize.
opsbot: alert mute created for alerts/5xx-high by Jamal H. duration=20m reason="noise during active mitigation"
Kevin T.: pool rebalancer moved traffic, pool latencies dropping, 5xx down to ~3.1%
Jamal H.: good. I'm handing off to Alex for next 60m observation window — tagging @Alex P. for follow-up.
Alex P.: taking over. next steps: create a dashboard tile for per-pool 5xx % and a short-lived alert that excludes transient provider preemptions. Also add a runbook link to the alert.
Maria G.: can we also capture which API keys hit the issue so CSM can follow up?
Alex P.: yes, logs already include api_key hash; I'll export the list and DM Sophiel for customer outreach.
Sophie L.: got it.
Jamal H.: handoff note: paged due to increase from baseline (~0.5%) to 12%. Mitigations applied: routing away, timeout bump, fallback route. Current status: error-rate stabilized ~3% and trending down.
Alex P.: post-incident tuning proposals: 
- Lower noise: change alert to trigger when 5xx >= 5% for 5m (was 1% for 1m) for service-level paging.
- Add per-route 5xx alert to catch regressions without paging for whole gateway.
- Add exclusion filter for known provider preemption events: `provider_event:true` in logs to avoid false positives.
- Dashboard: per-pool 90th latency, 5xx %, and active connections; add color band for provider preemption windows.
Suggested alert query (PromQL-like):
```
(sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="gateway",code=~"5.."}[5m])) by (route) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="gateway"}[5m])) by (route)) * 100 > 5
```
Alex P.: also recommend an automated short-circuit: when pool latency > 1s and 5xx > 8% route to fallback model for that route.
Kevin T.: infra action: open a ticket with provider ops for spot churn patterns; if they confirm preemptions, we'll add provider-native metrics to our dashboards.
Maria G.: tracking action items for comms: if >5% customers affected or >30m persistent, prepare customer-facing update.
Jamal H.: recording runbook note: updated runbook -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/5xx-handling (temporary changes documented)
Alex P.: I'll keep monitoring and will escalate to SRE if error-rate creeps back above 6% for 10m.
opsbot: incident resolved as of 10:28Z — status: mitigation in place, monitoring.
Sophie L.: sent interim notices to affected customers; no escalations so far.
Alex P.: follow-up items (track in #eng-sre): 
- Change alert thresholds (5% over 5m) and add per-route alerts
- Create dashboard tile for pool-level 5xx and latency
- Add provider preemption signal to logs and alert filters
- Add guard in routing to fallback models when pool lat >1s and 5xx>8%
Jamal H.: thanks all — reopening PD incident if it resurfaces.
Maria G.: filing a short post-incident note for PMs; will include customer impact summary and timeline.
Alex P.: marking this thread as done for now, will post a short postmortem if needed. :white_check_mark:
